title: Nvidia Just Launched a Chip That Puts a Supercomputer Inside a Laptop. AMD and Intel Dropped Immediately.
excerpt: The RTX Spark, unveiled at Computex with Microsoft, delivers 1 petaflop of AI on a laptop. Jensen Huang says the 40-year-old PC is being reinvented. For NRI tech investors, the winners and losers are already clear.
body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stood on stage at Computex in Taipei on Monday and made a declaration that investors took seriously: the personal computer is being reinvented. Hours later, Nvidia shares were up 1.6 per cent in premarket trading. AMD fell 3.4 per cent. Intel dropped 2.9 per cent. The reshuffling of the chip market's most contested territory had begun.

## What Nvidia Announced

The RTX Spark is a single chip — Nvidia calls it a "superchip" — that combines a Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and fifth-generation Tensor Cores alongside a 20-core Grace CPU, connected via Nvidia's proprietary NVLink chip-to-chip interconnect. MediaTek, the Taiwanese semiconductor company, collaborated on the CPU design.

The headline specification: 1 petaflop of AI performance in a laptop form factor. That is the kind of computing power that was confined to data centres two years ago. The chip supports up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory, which means it can run large language models — the same class of AI that powers ChatGPT and its competitors — locally, without an internet connection.

Huang was explicit about the strategic intent. "For forty years, you launched apps. Click. Type. With RTX Spark and Microsoft Windows, you ask — and the PC does the work," he said. "This is the new PC. The personal AI computer."

Microsoft's Pavan Davuluri, who leads Windows and Devices, appeared alongside Huang to confirm that RTX Spark-powered laptops and desktops will run Windows and ship this autumn from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface, and MSI, with Acer and GIGABYTE to follow.

Adobe is rearchitecting Photoshop and Premiere Pro for the chip, claiming a 2x improvement in AI and graphics performance. The pitch is that creative professionals — designers, video editors, 3D artists — will be able to run AI-intensive workflows on a thin laptop with all-day battery life instead of a bulky desktop or a cloud subscription.

## Why AMD and Intel Dropped

The market reaction was swift because the RTX Spark does not merely enter the PC chip market — it redefines what a PC chip is supposed to do.

AMD and Intel have built their businesses around central processors (CPUs) that handle general computing tasks. Nvidia has built its business around graphics processors (GPUs) that handle parallel workloads — gaming, scientific computing, and now AI. The RTX Spark combines both into one chip, directly challenging AMD's Ryzen AI and Intel's Core Ultra processors on their home turf.

The threat is structural. If the "AI PC" becomes the default category — and both Microsoft and Nvidia are betting everything on that premise — then the value proposition of a standalone CPU diminishes. The chip that runs AI best wins, and Nvidia's lead in AI silicon is measured in years, not quarters.

Industry analyst Neil Shah of Counterpoint Research called it a potential inflection point: "This is going to be the RTX Spark moment for the personal computing segment like how iPhone, ChatGPT, or DeepSeek have been."

Nvidia also unveiled the Vera CPU, a standalone central processor designed specifically for AI agents. Early adopters include OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX — a list that signals server-grade ambitions beyond the consumer PC market.

## The Broader Market Context

The RTX Spark announcement landed on the first trading day of June, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both entering the month at record highs. The S&P 500 has logged its ninth consecutive weekly gain — its longest streak of the year — and has set 26 closing highs in 2026 so far.

Wall Street futures were modestly higher on Monday morning, with the Dow up 143 points and the S&P 500 up 17.5 points in premarket. The mood was cautiously optimistic, though oil prices rose on the back of renewed US-Iran tensions, and traders still price a nearly 70 per cent probability of a quarter-point rate hike before year end.

The week ahead is dense with catalysts. Broadcom reports earnings on Wednesday — the second-largest US chipmaker by market value after Nvidia. Friday brings the May jobs report, a critical data point before Kevin Warsh's debut policy meeting as Fed Chair later this month. A slew of Fed officials will speak throughout the week before the pre-meeting blackout period begins Saturday.

## What NRI Tech Investors Should Consider

For the estimated 2.3 million Indian-born tech professionals working in the United States — many of whom hold concentrated positions in technology stocks through employer equity plans and personal portfolios — the RTX Spark announcement clarifies a trend that has been building for two years.

Nvidia's total market capitalisation now exceeds $5 trillion. It is the world's most valuable company by that measure. The company has expanded from a GPU maker for gamers into the foundational infrastructure provider for the entire AI industry — from data centres to, now, personal computers. Each new product announcement extends the moat.

AMD, which had been positioning its Ryzen AI line as the AI PC alternative, faces a direct competitive challenge from a company with deeper AI software integration (CUDA, TensorRT, DLSS) and a proven developer ecosystem. Intel, still restructuring under its turnaround plan, now confronts a third front of competition beyond servers and traditional PCs.

For portfolio allocation, the question is straightforward: the AI PC category is being created in real time, and Nvidia is defining it. Whether that justifies current valuations — Nvidia trades at a substantial premium to semiconductor peers — depends on execution. But the direction of the market is no longer ambiguous.

**Sources:** Reuters (June 1, 2026), Nvidia/GlobeNewsWire (Computex announcement), Counterpoint Research, Investors Business Daily, AInvest
